correctness.rationale: After normalization, a constrained maximizer of the local complex zero-sum sixth moment satisfies a common Lagrange equation. The nonzero multiplier branch forces all coordinates to one real line; a strict convexity argument in the third elementary symmetric function eliminates three distinct values; the remaining two-value family has objective Phi_m(t)=m^2/t^2-5/t+5/m^2, strictly decreasing on the feasible range, so multiplicities 1 and m-1 are forced. Summing this sharp lemma over annihilator cosets and tracking equality yields the exact Fourier constant and the full extremizer class. verifier.py exactly checks the Newton identity, all two-value multiplicities for 2<=m<=200, the algebraic scaling identity, and the equality vectors; random tests are only regression checks.

value.rationale: Finite complements of subgroups are a canonical structured test family for Lambda(p) constants. The sixth moment is mathematically distinct from the known fourth-moment calculation: its sharpness depends on a nonlinear complex zero-sum extremal problem. The theorem supplies an exact constant for every group and subgroup size, all equality cases, and a reusable sharp local lemma, so it is more than a routine parameter substitution or finite computation.
